fE0W9UGzZzk.title: people are lying about agentic coding

speakers.name: Lars Faye
speakers.role: Independent developer, YouTuber and essayist, skeptic of fully autonomous agentic coding

fE0W9UGzZzk.summary: Lars Faye argues that the industry narrative that 'coding is solved' conflicts with the reality that agents need detailed specs, rigid feedback loops, strong verification and architectural pipelines, all of which demand domain expertise. He says developers who struggle are told 'skill issue', which feels like gaslighting. He advocates using agents as a delegation layer while staying close to the code, optimizing for doing better rather than faster.
fE0W9UGzZzk.perspective: Skeptical, experienced independent developer who uses AI tools as a delegation layer and keeps reading and writing code

fHWFF_pnqDk.title: Vibe coding in prod | Code w/ Claude

speakers.name: Eric
speakers.role: Researcher at Anthropic focused on coding agents; co-author of 'Building Effective Agents'

He backs this with a 22,000-line change merged into Anthropic's production RL codebase.
fHWFF_pnqDk.perspective: Anthropic researcher and builder of coding agents, pro-delegation but pragmatic about risk

fQmlML9Lay4.title: Conductor CEO Charlie Holtz Walks Us Through His AI Coding Setup

speakers.role: Co-founder/CEO of Conductor (YC S24), a Mac app for orchestrating parallel coding agents

fQmlML9Lay4.perspective: Startup founder building a multi-agent orchestration tool and dogfooding it; heavy token spender, opinionated about UI and human-owned architecture

fabAI1OKKww.title: The complete guide to Agent Skills

speakers.role: Developer advocate for GitHub Copilot / Visual Studio Code

The video shows how to build a hello-world skill, then uses Anthropic's PDF skill to teach the agent a capability it lacked, and ends with guidance on skills vs instructions vs prompt files vs custom agents.
fabAI1OKKww.perspective: Tool vendor developer advocate (GitHub Copilot / VS Code) giving a practical tutorial

gv0WHhKelSE.title: Claude Code best practices | Code w/ Claude

speakers.name: Cal Rueb
speakers.role: Member of Technical Staff, Anthropic Applied AI; core contributor to Claude Code (prompts, tools, evals)

gv0WHhKelSE.summary: An Anthropic engineer explains how Claude Code works as a 'pure agent' (instructions, tools, loop, agentic search with no indexing), then walks through use cases and best practices: CLAUDE.md, permissions, CLI tools over MCP, context management, plan-first workflows, TDD/linting/commits, parallel sessions, escape, headless automation, and new Claude 4 features like interleaved thinking.
gv0WHhKelSE.perspective: Insider on the Claude Code team, working on system prompts, tool descriptions, and evals, speaking in the early days of Claude Code (Claude 4 launch).

hy8UstR2NEg.title: Full Course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents

speakers.name: Paul Everett
speakers.role: Developer advocate at JetBrains, course instructor

It also covers replanning, brownfield adoption, skills, MCP vs CLI, plugins and agent-portability standards. The main argument is that specs, not chat history, should be the durable memory and contract between human and agent.
hy8UstR2NEg.perspective: Tool-vendor educators (JetBrains + DeepLearning.AI) teaching a structured, human-in-the-loop SDD workflow using Claude Code and WebStorm

iQyg-KypKAA.title: L8 Principal's Agentic Engineering Workflow

speakers.name: Kun Chen
speakers.role: Former L8 principal engineer (Meta, Microsoft, Atlassian), builds frontier coding agents, independent builder of open-source agent tooling (lavish, no-mistakes, good night have fun, treehouse, first mate, AXI)

iQyg-KypKAA.summary: A full walkthrough of Kun Chen's terminal-centric agentic engineering workflow, framed as a captain building a crew: set up the environment, onboard agents with memory files and skills, work with one agent (voice, visual planning, automated validation pipeline), scale to parallel agents with worktrees, then delegate orchestration to a 'first mate' agent. The core argument is that engineers should act like engineering managers: spend time at the start (requirements) and end (quality bar) of tasks, and automate everything in the middle.
iQyg-KypKAA.perspective: Senior/principal engineer and tool builder who ships 40-50 PRs a day with agents and open-sources his own agent tooling

julbw1JuAz0.title: Building Claude Code with Boris Cherny

speakers.name: Boris Cherny
speakers.role: Creator and engineering lead of Claude Code at Anthropic; ex-Meta (7 years, led code quality)

julbw1JuAz0.summary: Boris Cherny describes how Claude Code grew from a terminal side project into a major developer tool, and how he now ships 20-30 PRs a day with no handwritten code. He covers his parallel-agent workflow, layered code review and security, prototyping instead of writing PRDs, and agent teams. He closes with a printing-press analogy for where software engineering is heading and which skills still matter.
julbw1JuAz0.perspective: Builder of Claude Code and former Meta code-quality lead; a practitioner-optimist who also stresses safety and humility

kwSVtQ7dziU.title: Skill Issue: Andrej Karpathy on Code Agents, AutoResearch, and the Loopy Era of AI

speakers.name: Andrej Karpathy
speakers.role: AI researcher, former Tesla AI director and OpenAI founding member, creator of nanoGPT/nanochat/autoresearch, Eureka Labs

kwSVtQ7dziU.summary: Karpathy describes how, since December 2025, he has shifted from writing code himself to delegating almost everything to coding agents, and how he now treats his own role as the bottleneck to remove. lXUZvyajciY.title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

speakers.name: Andrej Karpathy
speakers.role: AI researcher, ex-OpenAI founding member, ex-Tesla AI lead, founder of Eureka Labs, author of nanochat

lXUZvyajciY.summary: Karpathy argues this is the 'decade of agents', not the year, because current LLM agents still lack continual learning, multimodality and real cognitive depth. lXUZvyajciY.perspective: Veteran AI researcher and practitioner, pragmatic and somewhat skeptical of hype; hands-on user of Claude Code, Codex and GPT-5 Pro; educator

mR-WAvEPRwE.title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

speakers.role: Applied AI engineer, Anthropic

speakers.name: Andrew Wilson
speakers.role: Applied AI engineer / solution architect, Anthropic (London)

mR-WAvEPRwE.summary: Two Anthropic applied AI engineers explain how to build agents that run for hours. mWvtOHlZM-I.title: Tool, skill, or subagent? Decomposing an agent that outgrew its prompt

speakers.name: Will
speakers.role: Engineer on Applied AI team at Anthropic

n97BCfyFIvw.title: "The engineer of the future is the person who is able to choose what is worth doing." — Addy Osmani

speakers.name: Addy Osmani
speakers.role: Engineer at Google (Chrome), author, speaker at AI Engineer

n97BCfyFIvw.summary: Osmani argues that as agents take over the inner execution loop (harnesses, loops, software factories), the scarce human contribution becomes judgment, evidence, and accountability. o6oYc9-X9Iw.title: Agentic coding at Airbnb

speakers.role: Engineer, Developer Platform at Airbnb (~two decades building developer tools, open source author)

o6oYc9-X9Iw.perspective: Developer-platform/tooling engineers at a large company (Airbnb) driving internal adoption of coding agents

ow1we5PzK-o.title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

speakers.name: Luke Alvoeiro
speakers.role: Leads core agent harness at Factory; previously started Goose at Block

ow1we5PzK-o.summary: Luke presents Factory's 'Missions', a multi-agent system that runs coding work for hours to days using an orchestrator, workers, and validators. ow1we5PzK-o.perspective: Builder of a production multi-agent coding harness (Factory Droid / Missions), formerly creator of Goose

owmJyKVu5f8.title: Simon Willison: Engineering practices that make coding agents work - The Pragmatic Summit

speakers.name: Simon Willison
speakers.role: Co-creator of Django, creator of Datasette, coined 'prompt injection' and 'lethal trifecta', prominent AI blogger

owmJyKVu5f8.summary: Simon Willison describes his current agentic workflow (writing most code via Claude on his phone) and the engineering practices that make agents reliable: red/green TDD, manual testing with tools like Showboat, conformance suites, and templates that seed good patterns. owmJyKVu5f8.perspective: Veteran open-source engineer and AI-security commentator who is a heavy daily practitioner of coding agents

pqlWNihgdjI.title: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native: Building a Frontier Development Team — Clare Liguori, AWS

speakers.name: Clare Liguori
speakers.role: Senior Principal Engineer at AWS, works on Kiro (agentic coding assistant)

pqlWNihgdjI.summary: Liguori describes 'frontier development' inside Amazon: engineers write 1-2% of code by hand, run agents for hours, and run many in parallel. pqlWNihgdjI.perspective: AWS senior principal engineer and Kiro builder reporting on internal Amazon pilots

qyPCVqFUyDo.title: Boris Cherny: We Cut 80% of Claude Code’s Prompt

speakers.name: Boris Cherny
speakers.role: Creator of Claude Code at Anthropic

qyPCVqFUyDo.summary: Boris Cherny discusses the Opus 5 release and how Claude Code's harness is rebuilt with each model: deleting 80% of the system prompt, using ablations, and giving models harder tasks with verification. He covers product overhang, long-running jobs (an 11-day Zig-to-Rust Bun rewrite, a 2-week Swift rewrite), dynamic workflows with thousands of agents, and self-maintaining routines. qyPCVqFUyDo.perspective: Builder of Claude Code at Anthropic, speaking to a startup-founder audience

rmvDxxNubIg.title: No Vibes Allowed: Solving Hard Problems in Complex Codebases – Dex Horthy, HumanLayer

speakers.name: Dex Horthy
speakers.role: Founder/CEO of HumanLayer, author of '12 Factor Agents', originator of the term 'context engineering'

rmvDxxNubIg.summary: Dex Horthy argues that AI coding agents fail in complex brownfield codebases because of poor context management, and presents a Research-Plan-Implement workflow built on 'frequent intentional compaction' to stay in the 'smart zone' of the context window. He stresses that humans must not outsource thinking: reviewing research and plans is the highest-leverage human activity and keeps teams mentally aligned.
rmvDxxNubIg.perspective: Startup founder and practitioner building agent tooling who rewired his team's workflow around context engineering, speaking from hands-on brownfield experience

rnDm57Py54A.title: Building your own software factory — Eric Zakariasson, Cursor

speakers.name: Eric Zakariasson
speakers.role: Engineer at Cursor (developer experience and product)

rnDm57Py54A.summary: Eric Zakariasson describes how Cursor dogfoods its own product to move toward a 'software factory' where agents do most of the work. He covers autonomy levels, the primitives a factory needs (codebase structure, guardrails, enablers, verifiability), the shift from worker to manager, and Cursor's internal automations. A long Q&A covers code quality, team silos, enterprise risk, handoff from PMs, and roles.
rnDm57Py54A.perspective: Cursor engineer and heavy daily user of cloud agents, practitioner-level view with product plugs

sLSTM9znQNs.title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

speakers.name: Tibo Sottiaux
speakers.role: Leads the Codex team at OpenAI; formerly Google and DeepMind

sLSTM9znQNs.summary: Tibo Sottiaux, who leads Codex at OpenAI, explains how Codex began as internal research agents and why it was built in Rust and open sourced. He also covers how the harness and model co-evolve, how code review and maintenance are being automated, how the Codex and ChatGPT merge worked, and how the team uses Codex for everything internally.
sLSTM9znQNs.perspective: Builder and lead of OpenAI Codex (an AI coding harness), speaking from inside a frontier lab

sX1GYDHaCiw.title: Subagents & the Multiplication of Context Windows   Thorsten Ball

speakers.name: Thorsten Ball
speakers.role: Engineer at Sourcegraph working on Amp, an AI coding agent

sX1GYDHaCiw.summary: A short talk arguing that subagents matter because they change our relationship to the context window. Each subagent gets its own fresh context window, so noisy tool calls stay out of the main agent's context and only the final result comes back. Ball demos a search subagent, an 'Oracle' subagent backed by a different model (o3), and parallel subagents that edit files.
sX1GYDHaCiw.perspective: Builder of an AI coding agent (Amp at Sourcegraph), enthusiastic but explicitly not claiming subagents solve everything

shZgedW15vg.title: How Anthropic uses Claude Code: Agentic Software Engineering at Scale - Daisy Hollman

speakers.name: Daisy Hollman
speakers.role: Engineer at Anthropic on Claude Code; led design/implementation of plugins and agent teams; former C++ standards committee chair

shZgedW15vg.summary: Daisy Hollman explains how Anthropic customizes and scales Claude Code for real, large-scale software engineering. She frames the context window as the fundamental primitive. She evaluates plugin abstractions (MCP, skills, subagents, hooks) by whether they scale with 'don't pay for what you don't use', and describes running many parallel agents with worktrees, agent teams, /loop, auto mode and fleet view.
shZgedW15vg.perspective: Builder of Claude Code plugins/agent teams features at Anthropic; language/parallel-systems veteran focused on scaling agentic engineering to monorepos

uU5Gv2h8-9g.title: Claude Fable, Claude Tag, and Anthropic's Culture — Cat Wu & Thariq Shihipar ft Simon Willison

speakers.name: Cat Wu
speakers.role: Product lead on Claude Code at Anthropic

speakers.name: Thariq Shihipar
speakers.role: Claude Code team member at Anthropic

uU5Gv2h8-9g.summary: A fireside chat with two Claude Code team members about how their work has changed with newer models (Opus 4.8, 'Fable'), the launch of Claude Tag (a multiplayer, proactive Slack agent), and how Anthropic handles code review, evals, system prompts, tools, and security (auto mode). The main argument is that as models get better you should trust them with more judgment, remove constraints and humans from the loop only after building eval infrastructure, and push your ambition and product taste higher.
uU5Gv2h8-9g.perspective: Builders of Claude Code and Claude Tag at Anthropic, interviewed by an experienced independent developer

v3Fr2JR47KA.title: The Future of MCP — David Soria Parra, Anthropic

speakers.name: David Soria Parra
speakers.role: Co-creator of MCP (Model Context Protocol), Anthropic

v3Fr2JR47KA.summary: A state-of-MCP talk covering MCP's growth (110M monthly downloads), the claim that 2026 is about putting general agents into production where connectivity is key, and a framework of skills, MCP, and CLI/computer use as complementary tools. He urges client-side progressive discovery and programmatic tool calling, designing servers for agents rather than wrapping REST APIs, and previews upcoming spec work (stateless transport, async tasks, cross-app access, server discovery, skills over MCP).
v3Fr2JR47KA.perspective: MCP co-creator at Anthropic advocating a pluralistic connectivity stack and better MCP client/server practices

vKT59uoByXc.title: Why Coding Agents Keep Making Your Codebase Worse
vKT59uoByXc.channel: Beyond Coding and Agentic AI Foundation

speakers.name: Dex Horthy
speakers.role: CEO of HumanLayer, coined the term 'context engineering'

vKT59uoByXc.summary: Dex Horthy argues that coding agents still degrade codebases over time (citing SlopCodeBench), that most online agent hype and 'token maxing' is fake, and that realistic gains are 2-4x, not 100x. He lays out his team's actual workflow: small one-shot PRs, overnight 'janitor' bots, design-doc-first planning with checkpointed implementation, and reading all agent code before review.
vKT59uoByXc.perspective: Startup founder/builder of agent tooling for large enterprise teams; pragmatic skeptic of hype and 'dark factory' claims

wc8FBhQtdsA.title: An AI state of the union: We’ve passed the inflection point & dark factories are coming

speakers.name: Simon Willison
speakers.role: Co-creator of Django, creator of Datasette, coined 'prompt injection' and 'lethal trifecta', writes on agentic engineering

wc8FBhQtdsA.summary: Simon Willison gives an AI state of the union: models crossed an inflection point in November 2025 (GPT 5.1 / Claude Opus 4.5) so coding agents now mostly do what you ask. He distinguishes vibe coding from agentic engineering, describes dark-factory/software-factory experiments (StrongDM), and shares concrete patterns (red/green TDD, thin templates, hoarding working examples). He also warns about cognitive exhaustion and the unsolved lethal trifecta / prompt injection problem, predicting an eventual 'Challenger disaster' of AI.
wc8FBhQtdsA.perspective: Veteran senior engineer and open-source builder who heavily uses coding agents daily (Claude Code, Codex), a security-minded AI commentator and blogger

xUnRQ9vLXxo.title: Everything we knew about software has changed — Theo Browne, @t3dotgg ​

speakers.name: Theo Browne (t3.gg)
speakers.role: YouTuber, founder, developer building T3 Chat and a 'full stack cloud'

xUnRQ9vLXxo.summary: Theo describes his 'AI psychosis' journey through model eras (Sonnet 3.5 = tool calls, Opus 4.5 = long-running tasks, Mythos = orchestration). He argues developers must drop old habits and sunk-cost attachments (the 'skeuomorphic phase' of software), and shift ambition: what used to be a startup is now a side project, so build wider and attempt things that feel stupidly big.
xUnRQ9vLXxo.perspective: Veteran developer and content creator, enthusiastic AI maximalist urging engineers to think bigger and abandon legacy habits

yv8VZpov8bk.title: I'm using claude --worktree for everything now

speakers.name: Matt Pocock
speakers.role: TypeScript educator and AI coding course creator

yv8VZpov8bk.summary: Matt Pocock tries Claude Code's new built-in git worktree support (`claude --worktree`) for the first time. He explains how git worktrees work, shows that Claude wraps them with auto-named branches and lifecycle cleanup, and flags a gotcha: commits and pushes can land on main unless the agent pushes an explicitly named branch. He argues this makes parallelization nearly free, and that AI coding relies on old fundamentals like TDD and planning.
yv8VZpov8bk.perspective: Independent educator and practitioner, first-impressions hands-on demo; building a Claude Code course
